findings.message: the reactivity contract for solid-js has no entrypoint/export summary for imported export batch; solid-checker cannot tell whether it reads reactive values, takes tracked callbacks, or returns accessors, so code flowing through it cannot be certified
findings.hint: Add an export summary for batch to the package's solid-reactivity.json (reactive reads, callbacks, return kind); an empty summary certifies explicitly that the export is not reactive. See docs/package-contracts.md for the format.

findings.message: reactive accessor "count" is read directly in rendering function, which does not track; the read sees the current value once and never updates when "count" changes
findings.hint: Move the read into a tracking scope: JSX, a createMemo, or the compute function of createEffect(compute, apply). If a one-time snapshot is intended, wrap the read in untrack() to make that explicit. Solid warns STRICT_READ_UNTRACKED here in dev.

findings.message: accessor setter "setCount" is called inside owned scope Migrated; writes under a children-capable owner create feedback loops in the reactive graph, and Solid throws REACTIVE_WRITE_IN_OWNED_SCOPE here in dev
findings.hint: Derive the value instead of writing it back: replace compute-then-set with a createMemo. If the write is genuinely imperative, move it to an event handler, an action, the apply function of createEffect(compute, apply), or a leaf scope (onSettled, createTrackedEffect). Wrapping the write in untrack() does not help: the guard keys on the owner, not on tracking. For an internal reactive source only, opt in with { ownedWrite: true } in that source's creation options.
